production.note: US model years. Quote (Motor Authority, Stephen Edelstein, 4 October 2021): "due to start sales in the U.S. in spring 2022 as a 2023 model". Still on sale: Lotus's US site lists the Emira V6 SE: "The Emira V6 SE features a supercharged 3.5-litre V6 engine, paired with the coveted 6-speed manual gearbox" (lotus-us-emira-page).

body.note: 'an all-new mid-engine premium sports car'; fixed-roof two-seater, no open version.

configuration.note: 'Supercharged 3.5-litre 400hp V6' (Toyota 2GR-FE). The four-cylinder Emira is a separate variant.

drivetrain.note: The Drive's spec box: "3.5-liter supercharged V6 | 6-speed manual | rear-wheel drive"

transmission.note: Lotus: 'six-speed manual transmission as standard, optional six-speed auto with paddleshift'. Carscoops on the US car: "a standard six-speed manual ... but customers can opt for a six-speed automatic transmission for an additional $2,150" (carscoops-emira-us-price). The automatic is a torque-converter gearbox.

powerHp.note: Quote (Lotus release): "Developing 400hp, it's mated to a six-speed manual gearbox with a visible gearchange mechanism and hydraulic power-assisted steering." For the US car, Carscoops (Michael Gauthier, 1 October 2021): "This enables it to produce 400 hp (298 kW / 405 PS) and up to 317 lb-ft" (carscoops-emira-us-price); Motor Authority: "in the Emira it generates a peak 400 hp" (motorauthority-emira-2023). 298 kW x 1.34102 = 400 hp, so Lotus's figure is horsepower, used as published; Lotus does not call it an SAE rating, so powerStandard is Other. The Drive's spec box prints "Horsepower: 395" (thedrive-emira-2023); see discrepancies.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: Lotus's pre-production target. Weight-order step 3 (curb weight of the lightest-specification car). Quote (The Drive, Alex Goy, 7 June 2022, spec box for the 2023 Emira V6): "Curb weight: 3,097 pounds". Motor Authority (Stephen Edelstein, 4 October 2021): "a 3,097-pound curb weight in its lightest form" (motorauthority-emira-2023). Two independent named-author outlets give the same figure, and Motor Authority says it is for the lightest form, so it is a car with lightweight options; Lotus does not name them, and a standard car is somewhat heavier. No US curb weight for a standard car was found. Evo's specification table gives "1457kg (claimed)" (3,212 lb) for a UK car in a 2026 review (evo-emira-review), a different market and model year, not used. CarExpert (carexpert-emira-2021) reports the figure as Lotus's July 2021 target: 'Lotus is targeting a kerb weight of 1405kg in the car's lightest form' (1,405 kg = 3,097 lb).

discrepancies.reason: Units: 395 hp is what 400 PS would convert to; Lotus states 400hp, which Carscoops gives as 298 kW / 405 PS.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Lotus's 400 hp as published, matching 298 kW.

discrepancies.reason: Configuration, market and year: 3,097 lb is the US curb weight in the lightest form; 1,457 kg is Evo's claimed kerb weight for a UK car in a 2026 review.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 3,097 lb (US, step 3) and labelled it lightweight-options.

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 3,097 lb (The Drive, Motor Authority) is Lotus's pre-production target for the lightest car (CarExpert: 'targeting a kerb weight of 1405kg'), like an estimate, and it is not stated to be the V6. The first US model year is also provisional: Motor Authority says the car came 'as a 2023 model', while Kelley Blue Book lists the Emira only from 2024. A Lotus Cars USA specification sheet with a final US curb weight, or a major magazine spec panel, would replace the weight.
